Theme

Nature & food

petal noun

also petals, rose petal, flower leaf

classical

Plin. NH 21.16: differunt enim multitūdine foliōrum (of roses)
Plin. NH 21.17: paucissima quīna folia

folium, foliī n.

noun, second declension

a leaf; of a flower, a petal

Latin has no separate word: Pliny counts the “leaves” of the rose, and calls the many-petalled kind centifolia, hundred-leaved (NH 21.17).

Other words

  • petalum, petalī n. — a petal: the botanists’ word

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. petal

    From the Greek for a leaf or a thin plate. In Isidore and the medieval dictionaries it is a plate of metal; of a flower it is first found in the seventeenth century (Morgan–Owens, from the Oxford English Dictionary).

Examples

  • differunt enim multitūdine foliōrum, asperitāte, lēvōre, colōre, odōre

    for they (the kinds of rose) differ in the number of their petals, in roughness, smoothness, colour and scentPlin. NH 21.16

  • paucissima quīna folia

    the fewest petals (a rose has) are fivePlin. NH 21.17

See also leaf, flower, rose.

SourcesPliny, Naturalis Historia, ed. Mayhoff (Teubner, 1906), read in the Perseus Digital Library.

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. petal.
